players.product: optical fiber, fiber cable, and connectivity solutions for AI data center scale-out and scale-up networks; solar polysilicon, wafers, and modules

quarterly_data.signal: LAUNCH (the release's key takeaway reads 'Launch of'): Corning Contour Form Micro Cable, part of the Corning GlassWorks AI Solutions portfolio, introduced at ECOC 2026. It is a high-density micro cable that increases fiber density in existing pathways, improves cable routing and supports fast air-assisted installation, optimized for metro and long-distance AI data center interconnects so operators can maximize pathway utilization and scale on existing infrastructure. Corning states it enables up to 50% more fiber in the same duct, for a step-reduction in duct size; it is built on Corning's Contour fiber for a compact footprint with installer-friendly handling.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 50% more fiber in the same duct

quarterly_data.signal: SHOWCASE (on display at ECOC, not described as a launch): Corning Multicore Fiber Solution, an integrated fiber, cable and connectivity offering that packs four cores into a single fiber strand, giving four times the capacity per fiber within the standard 125-micron cladding footprint for AI data center network density. Stated installation effects: up to 75% fewer connectors, which reduces cable mass by up to 70% and helps cut installation time by up to 60%.
quarterly_data.figure: four cores into a single fiber strand; four times the capacity per fiber within the standard 125-micron cladding footprint; up to 75% fewer connectors; reduces cable mass by up to 70%; cut installation time by up to 60%

quarterly_data.signal: SHOWCASE (on display at ECOC, not described as a launch): Corning MMC connector with PRIZM TMT ferrule technology, an expanded-beam ferrule that integrates precision-aligned microlenses into the MMC connector platform so optical signals pass through a contactless connection instead of traditional fiber-to-fiber physical contact. Corning states it reduces connection complexity versus physical-contact solutions, supports high-volume scalability and faster deployment, keeps performance consistent and is less sensitive to dust, debris and field-handling variability; it is designed to support insertion loss as low as 0.5 dB.
quarterly_data.figure: insertion loss as low as 0.5 dB

quarterly_data.signal: ON DISPLAY (the release calls it Corning's 'established' portfolio, not a launch): end-to-end passive Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) and Near-Packaged Optics (NPO) photonics connectivity solutions that bring fiber closer to the chip inside the data center (fiber-to-chip connectivity) for reliability, bandwidth density and energy efficiency in AI applications. Named components: detachable fiber-to-chip connectors, bend-resilient fibers optimized for CPO/NPO architectures, and pre-assembled passive optical management trays that simplify installation and enable scalable deployment.

SHOWCASE: scale-up cable management system, a data center rack demonstration of high-density optical connectivity handling the cable demands of next-generation servers, GPUs, LPUs and switches as vertical connections within the rack increase; the cable jumper system runs in a protective pathway to keep cables organized and unobstructed. The compact three-tray mini-rack also features a CPO-enabled optical backplane architecture, using light-based connections placed close to the chip.

Scope of the ECOC 2026 showing: the innovations belong to Corning's GlassWorks AI Solutions portfolio (a new micro cable, a multicore fiber solution, next-generation connectors, and co-packaged optics systems for scale-out of larger AI networks). Corning technology is featured in several joint demonstrations, including live showcases of multicore fiber solutions and co-packaged optics systems, and Corning technical experts give presentations on AI-optimized data center architecture and advanced co-packaged optics systems. Claude Echahamian (VP and GM, Emerging Businesses and EMEA, Corning Optical Communications) said AI is reshaping network requirements across Europe and beyond, and that Corning's portfolio spans advanced fiber technology, data center interconnects, subsea infrastructure and fiber-to-home broadband.

Corning's role in the Lumentum / Qualcomm Technologies / Corning joint ECOC 2026 demonstration (announced by Lumentum): a board-level, massively parallel optical die-to-die (D2D) interconnect for AI scale-up, designed for future CPO and NPO implementations and extending D2D connectivity over multimode fiber links spanning tens of meters. Corning's multimode fiber glass ferrules provide the high-density fiber connectivity used in the demonstration, which the release says highlights the importance of fiber density as optical links move closer to compute devices and advanced packaging environments. Claude Echahamian (VP and GM, Emerging Businesses and EMEA, Corning Optical Communications) said that as optical links move closer to compute devices, fiber connectivity must support increasing density, precision and scalability, and that Corning's multimode fiber solutions and MMC connectivity help enable the demonstration.
